question: Claude.ai uptime ≥ 99% for the week of July 27 – August 2, 2026?

model.prompt_context:
QUESTION: Was the uptime of the claude.ai component 99.00% or higher for the week of Monday July 27, 2026 00:00:00 UTC through Monday August 3, 2026 00:00:00 UTC, computed using the Claude status page's own uptime methodology?

SETTLEMENT RULES:
1. You are an AI judge settling an information market. Determine the correct outcome using the data provided at the time of settlement.
2. DATA SOURCE: the Uptime History page at https://status.claude.com/uptime with the "claude.ai" component selected. Its HTML embeds a per-day data array (React props); each day is an object of the form {"date":"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z", ..., "p":<partial-outage seconds>, "m":<major-outage seconds>}. Parse this embedded JSON (the quotes are HTML-escaped as " in the raw HTML). Do NOT use the api/v2 endpoints — they do not contain uptime figures.
3. Window: the seven daily objects dated 2026-07-27 through 2026-08-02 (Monday July 27 00:00 UTC through Monday August 3 00:00 UTC). Total window = 604,800 seconds.
4. Sum across those 7 days: Sp = total of the "p" values (partial-outage seconds); Sm = total of the "m" values (major-outage seconds).
5. Downtime-equivalent seconds = (0.30 × Sp) + (1.00 × Sm). This mirrors the status page's own weighting: partial outages count at 30%, major outages at 100%. Degraded-performance time is not present in this dataset and is not counted.
6. Uptime percentage = (604,800 − downtime-equivalent seconds) / 604,800 × 100, rounded to two decimal places.
7. If the uptime percentage is greater than or equal to 99.00%, resolve "Yes". If it is strictly less than 99.00%, resolve "No".
8. Give your final answer as exactly one of the two outcome labels.

DATA SOURCES: Claude Status Uptime History (https://status.claude.com/uptime), "claude.ai" component, embedded per-day p/m data.

POSSIBLE OUTCOMES — select one outcome exactly and output NOTHING else:
Yes
No
